question.text: Under the PMLA, the term 'Adjudicating Authority' means:

answer.text: The Reserve Bank of India acting in its supervisory capacity
An Adjudicating Authority appointed under sub-section (1) of Section 6 of the PMLA
The Securities and Exchange Board of India
The International Financial Services Centres Authority

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines Adjudicating Authority as an Adjudicating Authority appointed under sub-section (1) of Section 6 of the PMLA. It is a quasi-judicial body within the PMLA enforcement framework. The Trap: RBI, SEBI, and IFSCA are sectoral regulators and do not function as the PMLA Adjudicating Authority. The Adjudicating Authority is a distinct quasi-judicial body created under Section 6. Note: Appeals against the Adjudicating Authority's orders lie with the Appellate Tribunal under PMLA, and the workbook treats both bodies as part of the same enforcement chain.
